claims.text: A controlled vermicular eutectic microstructure can be introduced into a typical dual-phase HEA or EMPEA through tailored thermomechanical processing.
Changing straight eutectic lamellae into a vermicular morphology will simultaneously improve yield strength, ductility, Young’s modulus, and fracture resistance.
Conventional processing of relevant eutectic HEAs or EMPEAs generally produces relatively straight lamellae or rods.
A combination of directional solidification, controlled rolling, and annealing will induce kinking of eutectic lamellae.
Kinking straight lamellae into a vermicular morphology introduces additional phase boundaries in multiple orientations.
The additional, misoriented phase boundaries impede or pin dislocations.
Vermicular phase boundaries act as crack-deflection and crack-bridging sites.
The vermicular boundary network enhances strain hardening and toughness.
Multidirectional barriers to dislocation motion produce a more distributed accumulation of strain.
The kinked interface geometry arrests crack propagation.
The vermicular microstructure will increase yield strength by approximately 20–30% relative to a straight-lamellar baseline.
The vermicular material will have a Young’s modulus comparable to or higher than that of the straight-lamellar material.
The vermicular material will have lower crack-propagation rates and higher fracture toughness than the straight-lamellar material.
The proposed strengthening and fracture-resistance improvements will occur without sacrificing ductility.
Excessive grain coarsening or formation of brittle phases will prevent the expected property improvements.
Overly severe processing will reduce ductility, whereas overly mild processing will fail to generate sufficient microstructural modification.
The hypothesis is primarily applicable when a dual-phase eutectic structure is retained after processing.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis and falsification rule require an improvement in Young’s modulus, but the predicted outcome allows the modulus merely to be comparable to the baseline.
